s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain with systemic inflammation and neurological deficits
salient_findings: High fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain
Exposure to unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand
Worsening back pain and malaise despite initial antibiotic therapy
Development of weakness, numbness, and urinary difficulty
Inflammatory lesion of the spine with epidural abscess on imaging
key_facts: 1-month history of high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain
Touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand 1 month prior to admission
Initial outpatient therapy with oral cefprozil provided no lasting benefit
Admission laboratory studies showed elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Serological test for tuberculosis was negative
Blood cultures grew a Gram-negative bacillus on hospital day 6
Development of neurological symptoms including weakness, numbness, and urinary difficulty
Neurologic examination revealed grade 3/5 strength in the right lower limb and grade 4/5 in the left
Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess
Positron emission tomography–computed tomography showed osteolytic destruction of the neural arch of T9

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10

shortlist.label: Vertebral osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has osteolytic destruction of the neural arch of T9 and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Spondylodiscitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and progressive back pain

shortlist.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has osteolytic destruction of the neural arch of T9 and a history of touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand and symptoms of systemic inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's history of touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand, followed by a 1-month history of high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain, is highly suggestive of Brucellosis, which is a zoonotic infection that can be acquired through contact with infected animals or their products.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has an epidural abscess, this is a complication rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Vertebral osteomyelitis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is possible but does not fully explain the patient's systemic symptoms and exposure history.

rejected.label: Spondylodiscitis
rejected.why: Similar to vertebral osteomyelitis, this diagnosis does not account for the patient's systemic symptoms and exposure history.

rejected.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is also possible but does not fully explain the patient's systemic symptoms and exposure history, and the presence of a Gram-negative bacillus in blood cultures could be secondary to the primary infection.
